I would disagree with the proposed crosslink. To link this article with a lolFoundation Tale sort of ties the SCP with the lolFoundation canon. From a quick glance, the article does not seem lolFoundation and making that crosslink might make the overall connection rather disjoint.

Overall, let Roget have the final say if the link is alright.

It says on the MTF info page that SCP-574 is one of the anomalous that fall under the jurisdiction of MTF Psi-7. Turns out Roget wrote a pretty neat tale all about Psi-7 here. An in line link between this article and such a tale would work for a decent crosslink. As such, I am proposing the following edit:

Changing the following:

SCP-574 is located within Containment Site-105, which is surrounded by a concrete barrier three meters high and one meter wide. Warning signs are posted at the edge of the Foundation-owned property. Once per month, a live adult pig (Sus scrofa) is to be placed within SCP-574. Any additional buildings not being cultivated for study are to be demolished as soon as it becomes feasible.

To this:

SCP-574 is located within Containment Site-105, which is surrounded by a concrete barrier three meters high and one meter wide. Warning signs are posted at the edge of the Foundation-owned property. Once per month, a live adult pig (Sus scrofa) is to be placed within SCP-574. Any additional buildings not being cultivated for study are to be demolished by MTF Psi-7 as soon as it becomes feasible.

Admittedly, the linked tale in question is part of the lolfoundation canon, but there is no reason a main list article cannot serve as a means of delving into any of the canons.

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Strong core concept, solid progression, indication of sentience, overall a very admirable predator SCP. My only quibble is the Frank character, I gathered that he was somehow a servant of SCP-574, but this was never followed up or mentioned in the main body. If the SCP has a method of communicating with humans, or a way of manipulating them, I would think the Foundation would be investigating this. The Interview 574-A also left me confused at the end on whether Frank was consumed by SCP-574, or was still at large. Despite these issues I enjoyed the SCP and happily endorse it with my +1
